problem: The `plugins` namespace lists glob entries (`./plugins/*`, `~/repos/community-plugins/*`). Glob entries under `namespaces` are not expanded for the namespace: ProjectConfig.get_namespaces returns the literal pattern, NamespaceResolver.register_namespace logs 'Path does not exist: .../plugins/*' and registers the namespace with no paths (reproduced: resolver gives {'myapp.plugins': []}). The matched directories only reach the analyzer as plain package paths, so the namespace (and a `namespace:` scope on it) holds nothing. The example does not work as written.
replacement: List each repository of the `plugins` namespace explicitly (e.g. `"./plugins/core"`, `"~/repos/community-plugins/auth"`) and keep globs only under `packages`. Separately, file a bug that `namespaces` entries with `*` are not glob-expanded in ProjectConfig.get_namespaces.
subject: "./plugins/*",

problem: Every entry of the `myapp.plugins` namespace is a glob (`./plugins/builtin/*`, `~/repos/community-plugins/*`, `~/my-plugins/*`). Namespace entries are not glob-expanded (get_namespaces returns the pattern; register_namespace drops it as a missing path), so this use case configures a namespace with no repositories.
replacement: Replace the three glob entries with explicit repository paths for the `myapp.plugins` namespace (one per repository that holds part of it), matching the fix in the Configuration File section.
subject: "myapp.plugins": [

problem: Both commands need uv, but Prerequisites offers 'uv (recommended) or pip' and Install from Source offers `pip install -e .`. A reader who installed with pip has no working command here.
replacement: Add one sentence before the commands: "These commands need uv. If you installed with pip, register the `pyeye-mcp` command from that environment instead; the [entry points](docs/reference/cli.md) list it."
subject: `uv run --project` uses pyeye's checkout for the environment

problem: The previous section explains that pyeye analyzes the directory the server starts in, but Claude Desktop does not start the server in a project directory and this config sets none. As written, pyeye analyzes whatever directory Claude Desktop launches it from, and the page never says how to point it at a project.
replacement: Add after the JSON: "Claude Desktop doesn't start the server in your project, so give your project's path in each call's `project_path` (see the [tool reference](docs/reference/tools.md))."
subject: "args": ["run", "--project", "/path/to/pyeye-mcp", "pyeye-mcp"]

problem: A third-party config path, given as the only location although it is macOS-only (Windows and Linux differ) and Anthropic may move it. It needs checking against Claude Desktop's current docs.
replacement: Edit Claude Desktop's config file (`claude_desktop_config.json`; on macOS, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`; Claude Desktop's own docs give the other platforms):
subject: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

problem: The page's recommended install is `uv sync --frozen` and the server runs under `uv run --project`; `pip show` queries whichever pip is on PATH, not pyeye's uv environment, so it can report watchdog missing (or present) for the wrong environment. watchdog is also a required dependency in pyproject.toml, so a working install always has it.
replacement: Delete step 1 and renumber; start the list at "Check file system supports inotify (Linux) or FSEvents (macOS)".
subject: `pip show watchdog`

problem: A third-party UI command that may be stale. `/permissions` governs tool approval, not whether the server connects; Claude Code's `/mcp` shows server status and reconnects. Needs checking against Claude Code's current docs.
replacement: Check the server's status in Claude Code: `/mcp` (see Claude Code's MCP docs)
subject: `/permissions` in Claude
